# AIKit Operational Runbook (Universal Host Integration)

This operational runbook provides the unified command matrix for driving AIKit across all supported agent host clients (Antigravity, Claude, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline) under **PRINCIPLE-009 R7** (Pluggable Host Architecture) and **PRINCIPLE-017 R2** (Cross-IDE Synchronization).

---

## 🌐 Host Client Operation Matrix

- **Antigravity**: Native chat harness. Discovers this skill via `.agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` and rule files in `.agents/rules/`.
- **Claude (Code CLI / Desktop)**: Reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically on startup. Discovers this skill natively via `.claude/skills/aikit/SKILL.md`. Executes kit commands directly via terminal tool calls.
- **OpenCode**: Runs headless subagent profiles (`architect`, `coder`, `tester`, etc.) via `opencode run --standalone` and slash commands via `opencode.jsonc`.
- **Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf / Cline**: Loads `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`. Runs terminal commands.
- **State SSOT**: All clients interact with workspace state strictly through `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py` and `.agents/task_ledger.json` (a project's: `.aikit/task_ledger.json`).

---

## 🧱 Projects: Building Software Other Than AIKit (PRINCIPLE-011 R8)
The user's software lives in its own project, never in AIKit's tree:
```bash
python aikit.py list                 # which projects exist
python aikit.py new <name> --description "<10-350 chars>" [--topic <t>]... [--kind software|game|science]  # projects/<name>/: own repo, .aikit/ memory, AL-1.1/AGL-1.1/ASL-1.1 LICENSE + COMMERCIAL.md (ACL-1.0), Built with AIKit badge; topic aikit always added, title title-cased, description keeps its case; --publish (needs --description) uploads only these starter files with derived topics, only when the user asks
python aikit.py attach <path>        # an existing folder: adds .aikit/ memory and an AIKit Integrated badge under its README title (uncommitted)
python aikit.py status <name>        # its task, changes, latest decision and its gates
python aikit.py check <name>         # its Phase 4: tests, stack gates, hygiene, guidelines, secret scan; exit 0 to commit; never pushes, add --push only when push delivery is authorized (PRINCIPLE-018 R4)
python aikit.py guideline <name> "<rule>" --source user   # a project rule, below the principles
python aikit.py publish <name> [--public] [--owner <org>] [--license auto]  # its own GitHub repo with the README's description, stack/license topics and an AI-chosen license; needs a 10-350 char README paragraph; only when the user asks
python aikit.py license <name> [--suggest [--json]|--set software|game|science|--restrict]  # AL-1.1, AGL-1.1 (DRM-free games) or ASL-1.1 (science); --restrict, only when the user asks, makes later versions All Rights Reserved from HEAD (earlier releases keep their license), drops COMMERCIAL.md, blocks publish --public, and allows check --push or publish only to a repository gh reports private (ADR-214)
python aikit.py topics <name> [--suggest [--json]|--set <t>...]  # AI-chosen GitHub tags, recorded in project.json
python aikit.py fix <name>           # self-heals memory, cleans stale temp buffers, syncs codebase map
python aikit.py checkpoint <name>    # disruption checkpoint on the project ledger; --agent <host>:<session> names you
python aikit.py resume <name>        # disruption resume on the project
python aikit.py complete <name>      # mark project task complete; another agent's task needs --take-over
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --suspend "<reason>" --workspace projects/<name>  # pause a task, keep it resumable
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --resume-task <task_id> --workspace projects/<name>  # reactivate a paused or superseded task (ADR-219)
python aikit.py clean <name>         # clean dangling project buffers
```
- Request names no single project: ask which one, or the name of a new one, before writing code.
- Before writing code in a project, read its guidelines (`status` or `resume` prints them): its own rules, which add to the principles and never override one (PRINCIPLE-000 R6). When the user states a lasting rule for the project, record it with `aikit guideline`.
- In the steps below, project work replaces the repository with the project: use the cockpit subcommands above, or add `--workspace <project path>` to every `disruption_recovery.py` command, write ADRs in `<project>/.aikit/decisions.md`, stage and commit inside the project, and run `python aikit.py check <name>` as Phase 4. `aikit fix <name>` self-heals project memory and cleans temporary buffers. AIKit's other gates are for changes to AIKit only.
- The project check runs the built-in hygiene scan of its source and static assets: mark a deliberate finding `hygiene: allow <reason>` on its own line or the line directly above it. After the check passes, record the checklist outcome (`checklists: passed`, or the failed or skipped item IDs) in the task's latest checkpoint description before the commit (PRINCIPLE-001 R8, PRINCIPLE-011 R8).

---

## 🤝 Delegating to Sub-Agents (PRINCIPLE-008 R6, PRINCIPLE-012 R8)
- **Claude Code**: hand bounded work to the project sub-agents in `.claude/agents/` through the Agent tool: `explorer` (searches, haiku), `worker` (docs and boilerplate, haiku), `architect` (read-only design), `reviewer` (audits, runs read-only gates), `tester` and `coder` (sonnet). Brief each with the milestone, the files it may change and the commands that verify it; run Phase 4 on what comes back.
- **Other hosts**: `python aikit.py delegate <role> "<brief>" [--project <name>]` runs the same role through OpenCode, on free models only: `architect` and `reviewer` on Gemini 3.8 Flash (needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the environment), the rest on OpenCode `-free` models (no key). A paid `--model` is refused (ADR-132).
- Roles have one text, `.opencode/agents/<role>.md`; `python scripts/sync_principles.py` regenerates the Claude copies. No agent can Edit or Write a task ledger (`.claude/settings.json`).

## 🧭 Phase 1: Orientation & Cold-Start Recovery

### 1. Resume Interrupted Tasks
Run on session startup, cold starts, or after a context compaction:
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --resume
```
- If an interrupted task is found, resume from its recommended phase.
- If uncommitted files or orphaned buffers exist, inspect them before proceeding.

### 2. Disruption Recovery Audit
Inspect the entire repository status, active task, and dangling temporary files:
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --audit
```

### 3. Change Track Classification
Determine whether proposed edits require formal checklists:
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --track
```
- **Track A**: Zero edits / read-only investigation.
- **Track B**: Documentation, comments, and non-rule markdown. Requires Post-Flight checklist and secret scan.
- **Track C**: Code, rules, workflows, or schemas. Full lifecycle verification required.

---

## 📋 Phase 2: Checkpointing & Planning (Track C Gate)

### 1. Pre-Flight Checklist
Review before making any code modifications on Track C tasks:
- Freshness: Read target files in slices before writing (PRINCIPLE-003 R1).
- Call Sites: Grep all symbol references across the repository before refactoring (PRINCIPLE-003 R2).
- Zero Undeclared Deps: Only use standard-library modules or explicitly declared dependencies (PRINCIPLE-003 R3).
- Platform Parity: Use `pathlib.Path` and avoid shell-specific builtins (PRINCIPLE-003 R4).

### 2. Record Micro-Milestones
Checkpoint plan with explicit impact assessment (`--why`, `--benefits`, `--risks`, `--mitigation`):
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --checkpoint <task_id> --phase-num 2 --desc "[1/M] Planning and architectural design" --why "<motivation>" --benefits "<gains>" --risks "contract: ...; dependency: ...; concurrency: ...; state: ..." --mitigation "<strategy>"
```
- Bound milestone count to $M \le 6$ (PRINCIPLE-008 R3).
- Name yourself on every `--checkpoint`, `--complete` and `--reset`: `--agent <host>:<session>` (e.g. `kilo:2`) unless `AIKIT_AGENT` is set or you are Claude Code. A task another agent owns is refused (exit 1); continue it only with `--take-over` once that agent has stopped, and tell the user (PRINCIPLE-006 R7).

---

## 🛠️ Phase 3: Implementation & Synchronization

### 1. Synchronize Principles & IDE Instructions
After modifying `GUIDELINES.md` or `.agents/rules/domain.md`, update all 8 host client instruction files and README:
```bash
python scripts/sync_principles.py
```
- Verify zero budget violations (<1,750 tokens per target):
```bash
python scripts/sync_principles.py --check
```

### 2. Synchronize AST Codebase Map & Knowledge Base
After creating or refactoring symbols:
```bash
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py
```
- Verify link integrity and codebase map freshness:
```bash
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check
```

### 3. Subagent Delegation via OpenCode (PRINCIPLE-012 R8)
Delegate bulk token-heavy work to free or local subagents using headless non-interactive mode:
```bash
# High-speed grep and symbol exploration
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent explorer "<query>"

# Architecture & deep reasoning (SWE-bench 49.2%)
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent architect "<prompt>"

# High-fidelity code refactoring (SWE-bench 39.8%)
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent coder --file <target> "<prompt>"

# Automated test creation and regression verification
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent tester --file <test_file> "<prompt>"

# Documentation, link and claim-fidelity audit
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent reviewer "<audit_prompt>"

# Offline / Air-gapped code generation via local Ollama
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent coder --model ollama/qwen2.5-coder:latest --auto "<prompt>"
```
*(Subagents MUST NOT write to the ledger; only the root orchestrator writes checkpoints).*

---

## 🔒 Phase 4: Verification Gate Shield (Pre-Commit Delivery Triad)

Before committing any Track B or Track C changes, ALL gates must pass:

### 1. Test Suite Verification (100% Pass Required)
```bash
# Both tiers plus their per-test budgets (unit <=10ms, integration <=350ms)
python scripts/check_test_budgets.py

# Either tier on its own, when a failure needs isolating
python -m unittest tests.test_kit
python -m unittest tests.test_integration
```

### 2. Read-Only Quality Gates
```bash
# Rule and budget freshness check
python scripts/sync_principles.py --check

# AST and knowledge base check
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check

# Pinned license/catalog drift check
python scripts/sync_licenses.py --check

# Secret and credential scan
python scripts/check_secrets.py --all

# Invariant reachability shield
python scripts/check_reachability.py

# Universal operational dogfooding runner
python scripts/dogfood.py
```

---

## 🚀 Phase 5: Delivery & Git Operations

> **Authorization gate**: run Phase 5 only when PRINCIPLE-018 R1 authorizes the commit or push; when it does not, stop after Phase 4 and report the uncommitted files.

### 1. Mark Task Completed
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --complete <task_id>
```

### 2. Purge Dangling Temp Files
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --clean
```

### 3. Conventional Commit Validation
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --validate-commit "<type>(<scope>): <subject>"
```

### 4. Explicit Staging & Non-Destructive Recoil
```bash
# Stage modified files explicitly by name (NEVER git add .)
git add <file1> <file2> ...

# Commit
git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <subject>"
```

"""Read-only survey of every AIKit project: git cleanliness, ledger state, license, GitHub metadata."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1])
OUT = Path(sys.argv[2])


def run(args, cwd=None, timeout=60):
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
                       errors="replace", timeout=timeout)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.strip(), p.stderr.strip()


def ledger_state(repo):
    path = repo / ".aikit" / "task_ledger.json"
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"unreadable: {exc.__class__.__name__}"
    entries = data.get("tasks", data) if isinstance(data, dict) else data
    if not entries:
        return "empty"
    last = {}
    for e in entries:
        last[e.get("task_id")] = e.get("status")
    open_tasks = [t for t, s in last.items() if s not in ("completed", "superseded", "reset")]
    return "open:" + ",".join(open_tasks) if open_tasks else "clean"


rows = []
for repo in sorted((ROOT / "projects").iterdir(), key=lambda p: p.name.lower()):
    if not (repo / ".git").exists():
        continue
    _, porcelain, _ = run(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=repo)
    _, sb, _ = run(["git", "status", "-sb"], cwd=repo)
    _, url, _ = run(["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"], cwd=repo)
    lic = repo / "LICENSE"
    lic_head = ""
    if lic.is_file():
        lic_head = next((l.strip() for l in lic.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines() if l.strip()), "")
    slug = url.removesuffix(".git").split("github.com/")[-1] if "github.com" in url else ""
    gh = {}
    if slug:
        code, out, err = run(["gh", "repo", "view", slug, "--json",
                              "name,description,repositoryTopics,visibility,licenseInfo,isArchived,homepageUrl"])
        gh = json.loads(out) if code == 0 else {"error": err[:120]}
    rows.append({
        "project": repo.name,
        "dirty": len(porcelain.splitlines()),
        "branch": sb.splitlines()[0] if sb else "",
        "ledger": ledger_state(repo),
        "license_head": lic_head[:80],
        "slug": slug,
        "gh": gh,
    })
OUT.write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
for r in rows:
    g = r["gh"]
    topics = [t["name"] for t in (g.get("repositoryTopics") or [])]
    print(f"{r['project']:<28} dirty={r['dirty']:<3} {r['branch'][3:][:38]:<38} ledger={r['ledger'][:30]:<30} "
          f"gh={g.get('name', g.get('error', '-'))} vis={g.get('visibility', '-')} "
          f"lic={(g.get('licenseInfo') or {}).get('key', '-')} topics={len(topics)} desc={len(g.get('description') or '')}")

"""Read-only: license kind suggestion, version source, tags and commercial file per eligible project."""
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1])
rows = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
SKIP = {"MemoryReconstruction", "voidfarer", "fluid-universe", "ui-sandbox", "AegeanWorks"}


def run(args, cwd=None):
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
                       errors="replace", timeout=60)
    return p.stdout.strip()


for r in rows:
    name = r["project"]
    if name in SKIP:
        continue
    repo = ROOT / "projects" / name
    sug = json.loads(run([sys.executable, "aikit.py", "license", name, "--suggest", "--json"], cwd=ROOT) or "{}")
    version, src = "-", "-"
    for f, pat in (("pyproject.toml", r'(?m)^version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"'),
                   ("package.json", r'"version":\s*"([^"]+)"')):
        if (repo / f).is_file():
            m = re.search(pat, (repo / f).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
            if m:
                version, src = m.group(1), f
                break
    tags = run(["git", "tag", "--sort=-creatordate"], cwd=repo).splitlines()[:3]
    commercial = (repo / "COMMERCIAL.md").is_file()
    print(f"{name:<28} sug={sug.get('kind')}/{sug.get('confidence')} cur={sug.get('current_key')} "
          f"ver={version}({src}) tags={','.join(tags) or '-'} commercial={commercial} "
          f"changelog={(repo / 'CHANGELOG.md').is_file()}")

"""Move one clean project's new versions to an Aegean 1.1 license (generalized from the pilot).

Usage: python relicense.py <aikit_root> <project> [<project> ...]
Tags the last pre-change commit, rewrites files, leaves everything uncommitted for review.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
from scripts.project_license import apply_license_kind  # noqa: E402

LINK = "https://github.com/AegeanWorks/Aegean-Licensing/blob/master/licenses/ACL-1.0.md"
KINDS = {
    "software": {"key": "LicenseRef-AL-1.1", "name": "Aegean License 1.1 (AL-1.1)",
                 "short": "AL-1.1", "free": "personal use", "extra": ""},
    "game": {"key": "LicenseRef-AGL-1.1", "name": "Aegean Game License 1.1 (AGL-1.1)",
             "short": "AGL-1.1", "free": "personal play",
             "extra": "Game assets need a separate written asset grant; see ASSETS.md."},
    "science": {"key": "LicenseRef-ASL-1.1", "name": "Aegean Science License 1.1 (ASL-1.1)",
                "short": "ASL-1.1", "free": "non-commercial research",
                "extra": "Project Data and model weights need a separate written data/weights grant."},
}
OLD = {"agpl": "GNU AGPL-3.0", "apache": "the Apache License 2.0", "mit": "the MIT License",
       "al-1.0": "the Aegean License 1.0 (AL-1.0)", "none": None}
# project: (kind, previous license)
PLAN = {
    "chronos": ("software", "agpl"), "gauge": ("software", "agpl"), "lacon": ("software", "agpl"),
    "lattice": ("software", "agpl"), "merklock": ("software", "agpl"), "mnemo": ("software", "agpl"),
    "muse": ("software", "al-1.0"), "N1-Engine": ("software", "apache"),
    "NeuralBeat": ("software", "agpl"), "NeuralDeck": ("software", "agpl"),
    "neurocore": ("software", "agpl"), "NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR": ("software", "mit"),
    "NeuroOptic": ("software", "agpl"), "NobetWizard": ("software", "agpl"),
    "nomoreclutter": ("software", "agpl"), "pebble": ("software", "agpl"),
    "photo-harbor": ("software", "agpl"), "primordia": ("software", "agpl"),
    "tally": ("software", "agpl"), "tempo": ("software", "agpl"),
    "aldervale": ("game", "agpl"), "crypt-crawler": ("game", "agpl"),
    "cyberpulse": ("game", "agpl"), "fold": ("game", "agpl"),
    "PNN": ("science", "none"), "obezite-mekanizma-projesi": ("science", "agpl"),
}
COMMERCIAL = """# Aegean Commercial License (ACL-1.0) & Licensing Tiers

> This project is free for {free} under the **{name}** in [LICENSE](LICENSE). Every commercial or
> organizational use needs the paid **Aegean Commercial License 1.0 (ACL-1.0)**.{extra}{history}

---

## Tiers

| Tier | Who it is for | Terms | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Personal** | One individual, non-commercial use: learning, coursework, hobby projects, personal research | {name} | **Free** |
| **Commercial** | Companies and every other organization, freelancers, employees at work, hosting, paid client work | ACL-1.0, evidenced by a License Grant Certificate | **Paid, quoted**; one 28-day non-production evaluation per company group |
| **Restricted** | Projects withdrawn from distribution | All Rights Reserved notice from a recorded cutoff | Not offered publicly |

The binding text is [LICENSE](LICENSE); the commercial agreement is
[ACL-1.0]({link}).
Contact `aegean-licensing@proton.me`.
"""


def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    done = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          encoding="utf-8", timeout=60)
    if done.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed in {repo.name}: {done.stderr.strip()}")
    return done.stdout.strip()


def read(path: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Text with LF endings, and the newline the file used."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        raw = handle.read()
    newline = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
    return raw.replace("\r\n", "\n"), newline


def write(path: Path, text: str, newline: str) -> None:
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        handle.write(text.replace("\n", newline))


def version_of(repo: Path) -> str | None:
    pyproject = repo / "pyproject.toml"
    if pyproject.is_file():
        match = re.search(r'(?m)^version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', read(pyproject)[0])
        if match:
            return match.group(1)
    return None


def bump(version: str) -> str:
    parts = version.split(".")
    parts += ["0"] * (3 - len(parts))
    return f"{parts[0]}.{int(parts[1]) + 1}.0"


def rewrite_pyproject(repo: Path, key: str, new_version: str) -> None:
    path = repo / "pyproject.toml"
    text, newline = read(path)
    text = re.sub(r'(?m)^license\s*=\s*(\{[^}\n]*\}|"[^"\n]*")\s*$', f'license = "{key}"', text, count=1)
    if re.search(r'(?m)^license\s*=', text) and "license-files" not in text:
        text = re.sub(r'(?m)^(license = "[^"]+")$', r'\1\nlicense-files = ["LICENSE"]', text, count=1)
    text = "\n".join(line for line in text.split("\n") if "License ::" not in line)
    text = re.sub(r'(?m)^version\s*=\s*"[^"]+"', f'version = "{new_version}"', text, count=1)
    write(path, text, newline)


def rewrite_readme(repo: Path, meta: dict, old: str | None, tag: str | None) -> None:
    path = repo / "README.md"
    if not path.is_file():
        return
    text, newline = read(path)
    replacements = (
        ("GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later", meta["name"]),
        ("GNU Affero General Public License v3.0", meta["name"]),
        ("GNU Affero General Public License", meta["name"]),
        ("AGPL-3.0-or-later", meta["short"]), ("AGPL-3.0", meta["short"]),
        ("AGPLv3", meta["short"]), ("AGPL v3", meta["short"]), ("AGPL", meta["short"]),
        ("Apache License 2.0", meta["name"]), ("Apache License, Version 2.0", meta["name"]),
        ("Apache-2.0", meta["short"]), ("MIT License", meta["name"]),
        ("Aegean-E Commercial License", "Aegean Commercial License 1.0 (ACL-1.0)"),
        ("Aegean-E/AIKit", "AegeanWorks/AIKit"),
        ("for open-source use", f"for {meta['free']}"),
    )
    for before, after in replacements:
        text = text.replace(before, after)
    text = re.sub(r"(?mi)^\[!\[License[^\n]*shields\.io[^\n]*$",
                  f"[![License: {meta['short']}](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-"
                  f"{meta['short'].replace('-', '--')}-blue)](LICENSE)", text)
    if old and tag and "**License history:**" not in text:
        note = f"> **License history:** versions up to and including `{tag}` remain available under {old}.\n\n"
        text = re.sub(r"(?m)^(## [^\n]*License\s*)$", lambda m: note + m.group(1), text, count=1)
    write(path, text, newline)


def migrate(name: str) -> None:
    kind, previous = PLAN[name]
    meta, old = KINDS[kind], OLD[previous]
    repo = ROOT / "projects" / name
    if git(repo, "status", "--porcelain"):
        raise SystemExit(f"{name}: working tree is not clean")
    version = version_of(repo)
    tag = None
    if old:
        tag = f"v{version}-{previous}" if version else f"{previous}-final"
        if not git(repo, "tag", "--list", tag):
            git(repo, "tag", "-a", tag, "-m", f"Last version under {old}")
    apply_license_kind(repo, name, kind)
    history = f"\n> Versions up to and including `{tag}` remain available under {old}." if old else ""
    extra = f" {meta['extra']}" if meta["extra"] else ""
    write(repo / "COMMERCIAL.md", COMMERCIAL.format(free=meta["free"], name=meta["name"], extra=extra,
                                                     history=history, link=LINK), "\n")
    new_version = None
    if version and (repo / "pyproject.toml").is_file():
        new_version = bump(version)
        rewrite_pyproject(repo, meta["key"], new_version)
    rewrite_readme(repo, meta, old, tag)
    decisions = repo / ".aikit" / "decisions.md"
    if decisions.is_file():
        text, newline = read(decisions)
        lines = [f"## Licensing migration ({tag or 'first license'})", "",
                 f"- New versions use the {meta['name']}" +
                 (f"; versions up to and including `{tag}` remain under {old}." if old else "."),
                 "- Rights holder: AegeanWorks; commercial use under ACL-1.0.",
                 "- Counsel review of the 1.1 texts remains pending."]
        write(decisions, text.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n", newline)
    print(f"{name}: {meta['short']} tag={tag} version={version}->{new_version}")


for project in sys.argv[2:]:
    migrate(project)

### AI Brain (observe/suggest)

The `brain` module is the control substrate for a neocortex-style loop. It composes a real
self-model from live flows, module manifests, memory, knowledge-base, metrics and evaluation
state; failures are reported as provider errors rather than mock values. An in-process event bus
feeds a bounded cognitive scheduler, and `observe` cycles record state while `suggest` cycles add
pending proposals. Autonomous actuation (`auto`) is intentionally not implemented yet.

`GET /brain/state`, `GET /brain/events`, `POST /brain/start|stop|cycle|mode` and
`POST /brain/events` expose the substrate. `POST /brain/eval/run` runs the deterministic echo
suite (or a supplied flow id), `POST /brain/eval/baseline` promotes the last result, and
`GET /brain/eval/status` compares current against baseline. The brain is experimental and ships
**disabled**: enable it on the Modules page (or set `"enabled": true` in
`modules/brain/module.json`); even then `auto_start` stays false until you call `/brain/start`.

Outcome learning mirrors experiences into the shared memory store: `POST /brain/learn` records
an action outcome, `POST /brain/learn/consolidate` turns repeated **training** successes into
`RULE` skills, and `POST /brain/learn/recall` reports held-out precision, recall and MRR.
Consolidation also distils repeated failures into bounded `[avoid]` knowledge that a later
success does not erase.
`POST /brain/learn/suggest {"query": "..."}` returns the skills worth reusing and the past
failures to verify before retrying.
`GET /brain/learn/status` and `GET /brain/learn/experiences` expose the ledger.
`POST /brain/goals/review` is a read-only review of active goals: overdue, stale, low-clarity and
near-duplicate objectives. Evidence links are exposed by
`GET /memory/links/{id}`, `POST /memory/links` and `POST /memory/links/{id}/accept`; a
contradiction scan (`GET /memory/contradictions`, `POST /memory/contradictions/scan`) is a
deterministic prefilter that only creates proposals for review. Evaluation runs
also record their per-task outcomes, so the scorecard feeds the same learning loop.

While the brain is running, ordinary chat/flow executions emit an outcome through
`core/outcomes.py` and become `flow:<id>` experiences; evaluations opt out to avoid double
counting and `/brain/stop` disables capture (`capture_flow_outcomes` turns it off entirely).

Self-improvement is explicit and eval-gated: `POST /brain/improve/candidates` accepts a flow
operation list (or `/improve/generate` drafts one), `/improve/evaluate` runs the candidate on an in-memory
copy, and promotion requires an admin, a **perfect same-flow baseline** with provenance, a perfect
candidate and no latency regression. `/improve/rollback` restores the snapshot; `/improve/status`
reports candidates and quotas (configured in `modules/brain/module.json`). Every candidate names
an active goal (`goal_id`) or declares `goal_kind: "self_repair"` with a reason; the link is
revalidated at promotion and the goal becomes `in_progress`. `require_goal_link` (default true)
controls the operator path.

Evaluation is read-only by construction: flows with state-mutating or external-effect nodes
(tools, memory writes, messaging, calendar, subflows) are rejected with `UnsafeEvaluationError`
before execution. `POST /brain/eval/baseline` (admin) accepts only a perfect run.

Self-configuration is policy-gated: `/brain/config/preview` shows a before/after diff,
`/brain/config/apply` requires an admin, and `/brain/config/rollback` restores the snapshot
(newer changes for the same target must be rolled back first). Only whitelisted settings,
allowlisted modules and bounded brain options are editable; protected modules, API keys and
secrets are rejected, and `allowed_tools` can only be narrowed. Changes go to the configuration
ledger and `GET /brain/config/status`; the daily quota lives in `modules/brain/module.json`. A
configuration operation follows the goal rule: `goal_id`, or `goal_kind: "self_repair"` + `reason`.

The governance kernel derives a risk score from provider errors, evaluation pass rate, drift, a
one-hour window of blocked actions and a one-hour per-component error window, then runs in
`normal`, `degraded` or `safe`. Failed flows and evaluations feed the component window and a later
success cancels one entry, so an outage cannot hold the brain down. SAFE blocks learning writes,
improvement and configuration; rollback remains available.
`GET /brain/kernel` reports mode, inputs, windows and gates; `/kernel/kill` and `/kernel/reset`
require an admin. Leaving NORMAL starts a 60-second dwell during which a single clean snapshot
cannot return to NORMAL; a kill switch or manual reset bypasses it. Escalation follows raw risk
immediately; release uses persisted 0.1 smoothing and a stale value expires with the error window.
`POST /brain/drift/baseline` records a measured baseline for drift comparison.

separators and instruction overrides on chat input and knowledge-base chunks, credential shapes on
every surface, and verbatim system-prompt echoes on output. `brain_guardrail_mode` is `observe`
(default: report and count) or `enforce` (block an injected message or document, replace a leaked

A bounded trend detector keeps 100 pass-rate/provider-error samples, compares the last 20 with the
previous 20 once a day, and turns a 0.10 regression into a reviewable `repair_metric` proposal
(one per day, no flow edits). `GET /brain/trends` shows the window and findings; thresholds live in
`modules/brain/module.json`.

Brain audit identity comes from the request, not from an `approved_by` JSON field. Loopback and
test clients are trusted as `local` admins (or the optional `X-Brain-Actor` label). Remote clients
must present a token in `X-Brain-Token`: either `NEUROCORE_BRAIN_TOKEN` (shared admin override) or a
token from the actor registry. `GET /brain/actor` reports the resolved actor.

Actor management is admin-only (`GET/POST /brain/actors`, rotate/disable/delete). Tokens are
returned once as `<key_id>.<secret>`, stored as salted PBKDF2 hashes, and selected by key id so a
check costs one hash. Roles: `viewer` (read-only), `operator` (learning, reactions, evaluation,
cycles) and `admin` (promotions, configuration, kernel, baselines, actors). Protected operations
record the actor name.

`/brain/ui` is the local Brain dashboard: kernel mode/risk, health, cycle status, proposals,
reactions (dismiss/mute), evaluation controls and start/stop/kill/reset controls. It is linked
from the navbar when the `brain` module is enabled and refreshes every five seconds.

result.output:
## 🔒 Security Defaults

NeuroCore is a control plane with no authentication, so it stays local by default. Remote
access, the auto-reloader and secret-bearing exports are each an explicit opt-in:

| Environment variable | Default | Effect when set |
|---|---|---|
| `NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR` | project root | Store settings, flows, chats and calendar events, plus every data file (databases, decoder key, traces, uploads, brain ledgers), in one directory (Docker uses `/app/data`); unset, data files stay in `data/` |
| `NEUROCORE_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind another interface (Docker uses `0.0.0.0` inside the container) |
| `NEUROCORE_PORT` | `8000` | Bind another port |
| `NEUROCORE_RELOAD` | off | Enable uvicorn auto-reload |
| `NEUROCORE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | loopback only | Accept extra `Host` names |
| `NEUROCORE_API_TOKEN` | unset | Token non-loopback clients must send (`X-API-Token` or `Authorization: Bearer`); a non-loopback bind refuses to start without it |
| `NEUROCORE_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_REMOTE` | off | Allow a non-loopback bind without a token, only when an outer layer (e.g. a loopback port publish) already keeps the app local |
| `NEUROCORE_BRAIN_TOKEN` | unset | Required for all remote `/brain/*` access; send `X-Brain-Token`, optional `X-Brain-Actor` |
| `NEUROCORE_EXPORT_SECRETS` | off | Include secrets in the config export |

State-changing requests are rejected when their `Origin` is cross-origin (CSRF). Destructive
routes also require the exact `confirm` phrase, so an API caller cannot bypass the dialog.
Marketplace packages are extracted through a path-confined helper, and secrets are stripped from config
exports and masked in debug logs. Tool code runs in a separate worker process (never in-process)
with allowlisted imports, only the environment values listed in the tools module's
`env_allowlist`, and a network allowlist that re-checks every redirect and caps response size.
On NeuroCore's own port a tool may call only `/memory/goals` and `/browser_automation/api/`, so
tool code cannot change settings or install modules through the token-free loopback API.

Literature search is restricted to three allowlisted adapters (Wikipedia, arXiv, PubMed) in
`core/research_gateway.py`. Each request, and each redirect hop, must stay on that source's hosts
and resolve to a public address; responses are capped at 2 MB and 10 seconds, cached for a day,
and returned with the source, retrieval time, licence and a content hash. `GET /research/sources`
lists the adapters and `POST /research/fetch {"source","query","limit","persist"}` performs a
search; there is no fallback to an unlisted search engine or a spoofed user agent.
These are defense-in-depth Python restrictions, not an OS isolation boundary: do not run
untrusted community tools on a machine whose files or credentials you cannot afford to expose.

ALDERVALE - a 2.5D medieval RPG rendered entirely in tiny ASCII cells. Low-poly

## 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference

- **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.10 or newer (standard library only) and a
  dark-theme terminal that supports 24-bit colour (Windows Terminal, Terminal.app
  or any modern xterm). PLAY.bat opens a dedicated maximized Windows Terminal
  window, and the renderer scales with the window up to 260x110 cells - a bigger
  window or a smaller font (Ctrl+Minus) buys more detail, and at tiny glyphs the
  screen reads as pixel art.
- **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest discover
  ```
- **Run something now** (under 10 seconds):
  ```bash
  PLAY.bat    # Windows: double-click it in Explorer - one click, no typing
  ./run.sh    # macOS and Linux
  python -m aldervale --demo 9      # hands-free attract mode
  python -m aldervale --screenshot vista.txt && type vista.txt
  PLAY_WEB.bat                     # one click: browser game
  python -m aldervale --serve --open-play # browser game (same engine)
  python -m aldervale --serve --open # launcher: terminal / browser / Studio
  python -m aldervale --inspect .inspect # 19 PNG images + 17 control checks
  python -m aldervale               # terminal play (WASD, SPACE, E, I, H)
  ```

  In VS Code, open the project folder and press F5 (or the Run button) -
  `ALDERVALE: Play` and `ALDERVALE: Demo` configurations are included.

|---|---|
| Status, task and gates | `python aikit.py status aldervale` |

## The Tale

The Suncrest Amulet, hearth-stone of the vale, was stolen by the Bone Captain
and now squats in the old camp beyond the eastern woods. Elder Quill waits by
the village shrine; Bram hammers steel at his forge; wolves and worse patrol
the trees. Slay the Captain, bring the amulet home, and Aldervale will call
you hero. Full cycle: talk, accept, fight, loot, equip, buy, return, victory.

That is the tale the villagers tell. The true canon - the First Fire, the
eleven Keepers, the Captain's grief, the wyvern's vigil, and where the saga
goes next - is written in **LORE.md**, the Chronicle of the vale. Every story
change to the game builds on it, and **ADAPTATION.md** maps every canon
element to the exact file that owns it.

## Graphics

The renderer aims at dense ASCII art rather than flat silhouettes:

- a 19-level glyph ramp (space through `$`) shades every face;
- terrain has a per-cell material grid (sand, grass, forest, dirt, rock, snow)
  and a coherent two-octave texture grid; each material draws from a weighted
  16-slot glyph table, so grass shows tufts, roads show gravel, cliffs show
  broken stone instead of one repeated character;
- the sky has a warped 8x8 dither and three fogged ridges; water mixes
  ripples, foam, a faint sun/moon glitter path and calm troughs;
- near ground detail: grass tufts, tinted flowers, pebbles, broken rock,
  snow sparkle and shells on their own materials;
- every billboard casts a dithered contact shadow and a sun-direction shadow;
  campfires, gate torches, shrines and door lanterns light the ground;
- shorelines have wet sand and foam; chimneys smoke, birds cross the day sky,
  and a gold place-name plate (plus `N` on the minimap) names the area;
- sprite baking draws line art only on meaningful face boundaries (`|`, `-`,
  `+`), adds a metallic specular and a cool shadow tint, and the downsampler
  uses a smooth mean glyph with the highest-contrast cell colour so plate,
  cloth and blade edges survive;
- figures mix rounded primitives (ellipsoid helms and pauldrons, wolf body and
  head, skull and ribcage) with plate geometry, and internal line art is drawn
  only at strong material boundaries;
- cottages carry stone footings, timber braces, layered thatch, a capped
  chimney, flower boxes and a lit door lantern; wells have a pulley, rope and
  bucket; boulders are rounded ellipsoids;
- a deterministic clear/rain/snow cycle, persisted in saves, with in-world
  messages and a weather label on the location plate; rain cools the ground
  and leaves puddle glints, snow dusts it in pale sparkles, and both have own scenes;
- the default camera sits at 4.6 m with terrain line-of-sight pull-in, so a
  knight spans about 20 of 60 rows instead of 14; the sprite and portrait
  contact sheets make every model change directly reviewable;
- the inspect harness renders all of this at 132x60, 80x40 and 40x20 without a
  terminal.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Title: Up Down + Enter | choose a menu option (clicking it works too) |
| N C H Q | new game / continue / help / quit from the title |
| W S or Up Down | walk forward / back |
| A D | sidestep left / right |
| Left / Right | turn the camera |
| Right-drag mouse | orbit and tilt the camera (full 3D look) |
| Left-click | walk to a point; talk to what you reach; attack a foe in reach |
| Mouse wheel | zoom the camera |
| Hold Shift | sprint (drains stamina) |
| SPACE | swing your sword (backstabs deal +50% from behind a foe) |
| Hold B | guard: blocks most incoming damage, spends stamina on each hit |
| E or Enter | talk / open chest / pick up / pray at shrine |
| I | inventory (U use potion over a few seconds, E equip best) |
| M | toggle minimap |
| H or F1 | help |
| + / - | zoom the camera (keys) |
| ESC | pause (save & quit from there) |

## Command Line

```text
python -m aldervale [--seed N] [--width W] [--height H] [--fps N]
                    [--demo [SECS]] [--benchmark] [--no-color]
                    [--screenshot PATH] [--inspect DIR]
                    [--inspect-scale N] [--web-shot PATH]
                    [--web-dir DIR] [--web-query QUERY]
                    [--web-size WxH] [--serve [PORT]] [--open]
                    [--autostart] [--open-play] [--save PATH] [--version]
```

`--demo` runs a non-interactive attract mode (also works piped, for CI);
`--benchmark` renders 60 headless frames and reports timing (~23 ms/frame at
132x60 on a 2026 laptop); `--screenshot` writes one plain-text vista frame.
Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure (What/Why/Fix on stderr), 2 misuse.

### Seeing the game without a terminal

`--inspect DIR` boots the real renderer headlessly and writes the views a
reviewer or an AI agent needs to debug graphics and controls:

- nineteen PNGs: seventeen scenes (world, castle day/night, camp night,
  cottage, rain, snow, combat and menus) plus `15_sprites.png` and
  `16_portraits.png` for figure review;
- a `.txt` mirror per scene: the exact glyph grid, a colour-class map and the
  dominant palette, readable in any editor or terminal;
- `report.json` with per-scene fill/colour statistics and the results of 17
  scripted checks (walk, strafe, turn, sprint, guard, attack, potion, menus,
  map, zoom, orbit, click-to-walk, key mapping, respawn, buy, sell); the
  command exits 1 if any check fails, so it doubles as a control gate.

Menus clamp to the viewport: help and inventory wrap, the shop drops its
description column, and the title uses a compact banner on small windows.
`--inspect-scale 2` sets PNG crispness; write under the project (`.inspect/`
is gitignored).

### Studio: the accurate browser lens

The PNG writer uses a small built-in bitmap font and tinted cell backgrounds,
which is handy but not pixel-faithful. Every `--inspect` run also writes
`index.html` + `studio-data.js`: a standalone Studio that renders the exact
character/colour grid with a real monospace font on black. It has three tabs:

- **Scenes** - all captured frames, zoom and fit;
- **Models** - 8 models/poses at 8 yaws, 1-8x, grid, spin and a 4x2
  all-yaws turnaround;
- **Checks** - the 17 probe results.

Open the page directly, or capture it with headless Edge/Chrome:

```text
python -m aldervale --web-shot shots/knight.png --web-dir .inspect \
  --web-query "tab=models&model=knight&pose=idle&yaw=0&scale=4&shot=1" \
  --web-size 1200x1200
python -m aldervale --web-shot shots/village.png --web-dir .inspect \
  --web-query "tab=scenes&scene=village&shot=1" --web-size 1600x1000
```

`--web-shot` drives installed Edge/Chrome (override with `ALDERVALE_BROWSER`)
with no Python dependency. Its DOM text matches the terminal grid exactly, so
this is the authoritative view; PNG/txt remain for browserless tooling.

### Browser edition (same engine, canvas view)

```text
PLAY_WEB.bat                          # Windows: one click, browser game
sh play_web.sh                        # POSIX: one command, browser game
python -m aldervale --serve --open-play
```

`/play` runs the **same Python World, Game, HUD and renderer** as the terminal;
the browser only sends keyboard/mouse state and draws the returned chars and
colours into a canvas. The forge takes about nine seconds, then the game runs at
20 fps with WASD/arrows, SPACE, SHIFT, B, E, I, M, H, ESC, click-to-walk,
right-drag look and wheel zoom. Browser saves use `saves/aldervale_web.json`, so
save-and-quit and continue work there too. Both builds run the same simulation
step, so menus freeze the world, death offers respawn and the victory banner
appears in the browser exactly as in the terminal. The terminal version is
unchanged: `PLAY.bat` or `python -m aldervale`.

The server binds `127.0.0.1` only and keeps one shared session. It pauses after
20 s without a browser poll and resumes on the next request. Opening a second
browser tab attaches to the same game. Expose the port deliberately if you want
LAN play; there is no account system.

### Launcher: terminal, browser and Studio in one page

```text
python -m aldervale --serve --open
```

**START GAME** opens the native terminal game in a new console (Windows);
**WATCH DEMO** runs the attract mode; **PLAY IN BROWSER** goes to `/play`;
**Open Studio** serves the inspection Studio at `/studio/`. `--open-play` opens
the browser game directly, while `--autostart` opens the launcher and starts the
native game immediately. If a launcher is already running, the same command only
reopens the page. Ports below 1024 are refused; use `--serve PORT` to pick
another. Only fixed launch commands are exposed and `/start` + `/api/input`
require the per-process token.

## Technical Notes

- The renderer is a 2.5D composite: a per-column ray-march over the height
  grid (front-to-back with a hidden-row buffer) draws terrain, water and fog;
  entities are depth-tested billboards chosen from 20 yaw-baked frames per
  pose, baked at high cell density with silhouette outlines and flat-lit
  faces so they read as solid models rather than noise; emissive faces (fire,
  crystals, windows) bloom at night. The camera orbits and tilts freely, and
  clicking the world walks there by reading the depth buffer.
- Frames are emitted as foreground-only truecolor runs of changed cells, so
  HUD rows cost nothing and full-motion frames stay small.
- Everything is deterministic from `--seed`: terrain, village layout, spawns,
  and the rng behind combat rolls.

content.text:
All four steps are done for the 31 clean repos: renamed, given topics and descriptions, moved to the Aegean 1.1 licenses, committed and pushed. Every repo passed its full AIKit check before its commit.

**Renames:** 22 repos now start with a capital, for example `orrery` → `Orrery`, `prism-relay` → `Prism-Relay`, `aegean-licensing-ops` → `Aegean-Licensing-Ops`. The other 9 were already capitalized. GitHub redirects the old URLs, and the local remotes point at the new names. Local folder names are unchanged.

**Topics and descriptions:** every description is 310 characters or fewer (GitHub's limit is 350) and ends with the license line, e.g. "Free personal use under AL-1.1; commercial use under ACL-1.0." The `agpl`, `mit-license` and `apache-license` topics are replaced with `source-available`, and games also get `drm-free`. No repo has more than 19 topics (limit 20). I read every one back from GitHub to confirm. Orrery's old description was out of date (it said four worlds and terminal only), so I rewrote it from its README.

**Licenses:** 26 repos moved.

| License | Repos |
|---|---|
| AL-1.1 (software) | 20 repos. This includes N1-Engine (was Apache-2.0), NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR (was MIT) and muse (was AL-1.0). |
| AGL-1.1 (games) | Aldervale, Crypt-Crawler, Cyberpulse, Fold |
| ASL-1.1 (science) | PNN (had no license), Obezite-Mekanizma-Projesi |

- **Old-license tags:** each repo's last old-license commit is tagged, e.g. `v0.1.0-agpl`, or `agpl-final` where the repo has no version number. Versions up to and including that tag keep their old license. Repos with a version number moved up one minor version.
- **NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR:** clinics using it for work now need a commercial license. Releases up to `mit-final` stay MIT.

**Fixes that came up along the way:**
- **The three earlier pilots (Assay, Orrery, Prism-Relay):**
  - Their commercial-terms link returned 404 (`blob/main` on a `master` branch).
  - Their history note left out the tagged release itself.
- **Commercial-terms files:** the old AECL/Aegean-E terms are replaced with the current ACL-1.0 template.
- **README length:** three READMEs went over AIKit's 22,500-character limit.
  - **Merklock:** I re-aligned its file tree; no wording changed.
  - **NeuroCore:** I tightened a few sentences without dropping facts.
  - **Cyberpulse:** I moved its 43-command table into a new `COMMANDS.md`.
- **Merklock's rules:** they require a security-review note on every change, so its decision log records one.
- **Aldervale test:** it checked for the old `## License` heading; I changed it to the exact new heading.
- **ASSETS.md:** the game and science repos each got a real inventory instead of the template placeholder.

**On the later list** ([knowledge/repo_backlog.md](knowledge/repo_backlog.md)):
- **Skipped repos:** MemoryReconstruction, voidfarer, fluid-universe, ui-sandbox and AegeanWorks, which had uncommitted work or an open task.
- **AIKit's own license links:** `licenses/CATALOG.md` has the same 404 `blob/main` links as the pilots.
- **AIKit `license --help`:** it still describes the 1.0 licenses.
- **AIKit's README rewrite:** it leaves a blank line inside the file tree and duplicates an existing License section. I fixed the output by hand in every repo, but the AIKit code itself is still unfixed.

**Still open:**
- AIKit itself has 3 local commits for the later list and task record that aren't pushed. I can push them if you want.
- `tmp_pilot_migrate.py` still needs deleting by hand; that was blocked earlier.

I have finished some projects. Look what is left to continue. Also we have no business with AGPL.  Also there is some long descriptions that is out of the limits of Github. Start working. Also look at publish, release tags. We do not have anything to do with those AGPL!
I'll start by re-surveying everything, since some repos may now be clean. I'll also check GitHub-wide for AGPL tags and releases and for any description over the limit.

# Project Repository Backlog

Projects left out of the 2026-10-26 normalization pass: capitalized GitHub names, curated topics,
descriptions within GitHub's 350-character limit, and new versions under the Aegean 1.1
licenses. A project qualified only with a clean working tree and no open ledger task. Each one
below gets the same pass once its in-flight work is committed or reset. AegeanWorks makes no
release under AGPL-3.0, so the first three still carry an AGPL LICENSE that the pass replaces.

| Project | Why it was skipped | Pass still needed |
|---|---|---|
| `MemoryReconstruction` | 163 uncommitted files; open task `living-sanctuary` | topics (drop `agpl`), description, license |
| `voidfarer` | 8 uncommitted files; open task `postpush-polish-verify` | rename, topics (drop `agpl`), description, license |
| `fluid-universe` | 56 uncommitted files, 1 unpushed commit; open task `z3-koide-core` | rename, topics, description, license |
| `AegeanWorks` | uncommitted `docs/styles.css` | none beyond committing that change |

`ui-sandbox` (now `UI-Sandbox`) finished its task and completed the pass. `idea-catcher` is a
new restricted project with no GitHub repository and is out of scope.

## Follow-ups found during the pass

- `licenses/CATALOG.md` links to `aegean-licensing/blob/main/...`, but that repository's
  default branch is `master`, so those links return 404. Either rewrite them to `blob/master`
  (GitHub redirects that path if the branch is renamed later) or rename the branch to `main`.
- `python aikit.py license --help` still describes `--set` as AL-1.0, AGL-1.0 and ASL-1.0;
  `apply_license_kind` writes the 1.1 texts.
- `_licensed_readme` in `scripts/project_license.py` rewrites a commented `LICENSE` tree line with
  the template's trailing newline, leaving a blank line inside the README tree (after `ASSETS.md`
  for games and science). The pass removed those lines by hand in every project it touched.
- `apply_license_kind` adds a `## 📜 License` section beside an existing differently named
  License heading instead of replacing it; seven READMEs had two License sections.
- `extract_readme_description` in `scripts/project_publish.py` does not strip a UTF-8 byte-order
  mark, so a README that starts with one never finds its title and `publish` sends a later block
  (a table, for `obezite-mekanizma-projesi`) as the description. That README's mark was removed.
- `publish` takes the README's first paragraph and cuts it at 350 characters with "..."; aldervale,
  cyberpulse, NeuroOptic and NobetWizard had a first paragraph that was too long, empty or a URL,
  and were rewritten so the paragraph is one complete description.
- The Aegean-Licensing policy drafts still tell a maintainer to create a `vX.Y.Z-agpl` tag
  (`policies/PORTFOLIO-MIGRATION-PLAN.md`, step 2); the license texts keep their non-retroactivity
  and AGPL-incompatibility clauses, which protect the licensor and stay until counsel review.

content.text:
The three remaining old-license tags are gone (`mit-final`, `apache-final`, `v0.1.0-al-1.0`), and their history notes are removed from the README and COMMERCIAL.md files of NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR, N1-Engine and Muse. All three passed their checks, then were committed and pushed. No tag or note for an old license is left in any repo. PNN still has its `v1.0.0` tag; that version never had a license, so I left it.

**Should we rewrite git history? I recommend not.**

- **It doesn't take anything back.** Anyone who got a copy under AGPL, MIT or Apache keeps those rights; a license already granted can't be withdrawn. Copies are already out there: NeuralBeat has 2 forks, NeuralDeck and NeuroCore 1 each, and every fork keeps the full history whatever you do to yours.
- **It could hurt you legally.** Rewriting old commits so they show an Aegean license would misstate how that code was actually released. Your own Aegean-Licensing texts are built on the principle that earlier grants aren't revoked, and a falsified history would weaken that position in a dispute.
- **It's disruptive.** It means force-pushing about 35 repos. Every commit ID changes, so every existing clone breaks, along with the kept releases and the decision logs that cite commit IDs. GitHub can also keep serving the old commits by ID for a while afterwards.
- **What matters is already done.** The current code, READMEs, descriptions, topics, tags and releases all show only the Aegean licenses. The old license text is visible only to someone digging through old commits, and that's an accurate record.

If a specific repo really needs a clean slate, for example before selling it, the safer route is a fresh repository that starts from the current code in one commit, with the old one archived. Even then, earlier copies keep their old license.

def _fit_description(text: str) -> str:
    """
    `text` within GitHub's 350 characters; the 200 used before cut what `new --description`
    accepts (ADR-202). A longer one ends at its last whole sentence, else between words, so the
    published description is never cut mid-word.
    """
    if len(text) <= 350:
        return text
    ends = [m.end() for m in re.finditer(r"[.!?](?=\s)", text) if m.end() <= 350]
    if ends:
        return text[:ends[-1]]
    cut = text.rfind(" ", 0, 348)
    head = text[:cut].rstrip(" ,;:") if cut > 0 else text[:347].rstrip()
    return head + "..."

### ADR-226: Projects Carry REUSE Metadata From Creation
- **Date**: 2026-10-26
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The catalog identified machine-readable metadata as a gap: an Aegean license is a custom `LicenseRef-*`, and a generated project had no `REUSE.toml` or `LICENSES/` text for a scanner to resolve. A human-readable LICENSE alone is not enough for automated compliance.

The generated README tree lists `LICENSES/` and `REUSE.toml`. `write_reuse_metadata` is the single writer, and a tests cover new, switch and restrict.
- **Consequences**: A scanner can resolve the custom identifier without guessing, while `reuse lint` remains the external verifier. A mixed-license tree still needs per-file SPDX headers, and a third-party file keeps its own identifier. The policy does not change the license grant.

- **Blank line in the README file tree:** the rewritten LICENSE line no longer leaves an empty line after it.

- **Byte-order mark:** a README starting with a hidden byte-order mark no longer makes publish skip the summary (Obezite's case).

- **Long paragraphs:** text over 350 characters now ends at the last whole sentence, or between words with "…", instead of mid-word (Aldervale's case).

**Catalog links:** 16 links to the license documents returned 404 because they pointed at `blob/main` while the branch is `master`. I fixed them in Aegean-Licensing (pushed) and resynced AIKit's copy.

163	def title_case(text: str) -> str:
164	    """
165	    A display title from a project name: words capitalised, small joining words left lower unless
166	    first or last, and known acronyms preserved (`muse-ai-music` -> `Muse AI Music`). Only the
167	    author-facing title is changed; folder names, repository names and descriptions keep their
168	    spelling (ADR-218).
169	    """
170	    words = [word for word in re.split(r"[-_\s]+", text) if word]
171	    title = []
172	    for index, word in enumerate(words):
173	        lower = word.lower()
174	        if lower in _TITLE_ACRONYMS:
175	            word = _TITLE_ACRONYMS[lower]
176	        elif not (0 < index < len(words) - 1 and lower in _TITLE_SMALL):
177	            word = word[:1].upper() + word[1:]
178	        title.append(word)
179	    return " ".join(title) or text
